content: 1. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 3. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 4. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 5. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 6. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 7. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 8. Atazanavir and abacavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 9. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, the abemaciclib dose should be increased to the pre-inhibition level. Close monitoring is necessary. 10. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose adjustments. 11. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of acalabrutinib to 100 mg once daily is recommended when co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. Close monitoring is necessary. 12. Atazanavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. New-onset or worsening diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia have been reported with protease inhibitors. 13. Atazanavir increases the effects of acebutolol through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 14. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 15. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of adagrasib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided until adagrasib concentrations reach steady-state (~8 days). If steady-state is not achieved, concomitant use may increase adagrasib concentrations and toxicity. Alternative drugs are recommended. 16. Atazanavir increases the levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure and toxicity of DM1, the cytotoxic component. Alternative drugs are recommended. 17. Atazanavir decreases the effects of albiglutide, potentially due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 18. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 19. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of aliskiren by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 20. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 22. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of alpelisib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended. 23. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 24. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, reducing its solubility and plasma concentrations. Co-administration should be avoided. If necessary, administer atazanavir 2 hours before or 1 hour after these medications. 25. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ambrisentan by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 26. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended. 27. Atazanavir increases the levels of amitriptyline by an unspecified mechanism and by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 28. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 29. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 30. Atazanavir increases the levels of amoxapine by an unspecified mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 31. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 32. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, may lower atazanavir exposure. Alternative drugs are recommended. 33. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended. 34. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Aprepitant also increases the levels or effects of atazanavir. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 35. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 36. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 37. Atazanavir increases the levels of artemether by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased toxicity risk is possible. Alternatives should be considered if available. 38. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 39. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, reducing its solubility and plasma concentrations. Co-administration should be avoided. If necessary, administer atazanavir 2 hours before or 1 hour after these medications. 40. Atazanavir increases the effects of atenolol through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 41. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is necessary. 42. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 43. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse events, including hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. 44. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. 45. Atazanavir increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. 46. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternatives should be considered if available. 47. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days should be avoided unless the benefit outweighs the risk. 48. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of belinostat by decreasing its metabolism. Strong UGT inhibitors reduce belinostat metabolism, necessitating a dose reduction to 750 mg/m² when co-administered with UGT inhibitors or in patients homozygous for the UGT1A128 allele. 49. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates according to prescribing information. 50. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 51. Berotralstat increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor or titrate the P-gp substrate dose if co-administered. 52. Atazanavir increases the effects of betaxolol through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 53. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 54. Atazanavir increases the effects of bisoprolol through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 55. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 56. Bosentan increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended unless atazanavir is boosted with ritonavir.
